name: SemIf
description: SemIf reproduces the Jev-style semantic-decision interface with open models, reading typed option probabilities from a single forward pass instead of generating parseable text, with shared-state prefix reuse for fast parallel decisions on a local 4B GPU model, MLX, or in-browser.

name: mobile-jev
description: A standalone mobile agent that drives a real Android phone through the Mobilerun API using TypeSafe's Jev model for per-step decisions—no ADB—bundling a live React streaming studio, a CLI with preview/execute modes, verified demos, JSONL execution traces, and request-level latency breakdowns for reproducible evaluation.

name: YFarmX | Frontier Tech News: AI, Crypto & Quantum Computing
description: YFarmX is an independent news site covering frontier technology — AI, crypto, quantum computing, space and security — that pairs fully sourced reporting with explainer guides, reference indexes, live trackers for exploits, AI incidents and quantum threats, a briefings podcast, market data, and utilities like model comparison and a gas fee checker.

name: Jev Directory — 50 evals, 1328 community builds

name: The Jev Registry — a daily watch

name: Jev Apps, Libraries & Examples · JevList
description: A reviewed directory of 110 apps, libraries, integrations, and runnable examples built on Jev—TypeSafe AI's typed-decision model—where each guide explains what Jev decides, the shortest real setup path, and the exact upstream commit or commands checked.

name: jev-router
description: jev-router launches Claude Code or OpenAI Codex behind a loopback proxy that sends each fresh user turn to the model tier best matching its assessed complexity—fast to long—while preserving the CLI's native interface, tools, sessions, permissions, and authentication.

name: Benchmark Heaven — Model benchmarks & costs
description: Benchmark Heaven is an interactive cost–capability tracker ranking hundreds of LLMs across 119 benchmarks, computing modeled per-task prices from actual provider rates, caching and token efficiency, filterable by region, provider, lab, and data-use policy.

name: fast-jev-compaction
description: A Claude Code plugin and npm library that replaces lossy summarization-based context compaction with Jev-scored pruning — it keeps verbatim every tool call and result Jev deems still needed and drops or truncates stale ones, preserving exact file paths, errors, and constraints that summaries would lose.

name: jevmeter
description: jevmeter is a CLI that gives any video a live BS meter: it transcribes speech, scores every sentence with Jev's calibrated yes/no probabilities via presets (debate, earnings call, podcast, sales pitch) or custom JSON questions, flags dodges, and renders a postable 16:9 edit with highlights, hyperlapse, and scoreboards.

name: awesome-jev
description: A curated index of 71 open-source projects built on TypeSafe Jev's typed decision API, spanning SDKs for many languages, framework/MCP/database integrations, and developer tools that use calibrated judgments for code review, commit gating, routing, ranking, and automation.

name: Jev-Moderation-Bot
description: A Python Discord moderation bot powered by TypeSafe AI that deletes spam and scam links in real time, escalates offenses through configurable warning and timeout tiers, profiles members via `/profile` across metrics like scam risk and toxicity, logs actions to a mod channel with pardon/ban buttons, and learns from pardoned false flags to prevent repeated misclassifications.

name: jevusecases

name: awesome-jev-typesafe
description: A curated awesome list of 325 entries cataloging SDKs, gateways, coding-agent integrations, replicas, and real-world projects built on TypeSafe's Jev, a fast "System One" model that answers typed Choice/Score/Noul questions with calibrated probabilities instead of generating text.

name: Jev Directory — 50 evals, 726 community builds
description: A curated directory for the typesafe-ai/jev model bundling 50 runnable judge-model evals with exact experimental_evaluate prompts, 726 community builds linked to their projects and source posts, and a copyable agent capability pack for matching requests to proven use cases.

name: typesafe-computer-use
description: Drives macOS toward typed goals by reading the screen deterministically (OCR plus accessibility tree), asking a small TypeSafe classifier which action comes next, and calling an LLM only for free text—about 155x cheaper and 14x faster than screenshot-driven frontier models.

name: jev-search
description: A self-hostable Cloudflare Workers app that turns plain-language requests into Search1API queries across web and vertical engines, then streams Jev-scored, URL-merged links and snippets with visible relevance, editable source/time filters, caching, and per-IP rate limits.

name: jev-frontier-100
description: A 100-question four-choice benchmark comparing Jev against local Qwen3.5 models (0.8B–4B) under controlled thinking budgets, providing frozen questions, graded trial outcomes, paired bootstrap intervals, confidence diagnostics, and an offline harness to recompute all published scores.

name: pg-jev
description: pg-jev is a PostgreSQL extension that lets you filter, rank, and classify table rows with plain-language conditions via SQL functions (`jev`, `jev_prob`, `jev_score`, `jev_choice`) backed by TypeSafe's Jev model, which returns calibrated probabilities per row—using batched API requests, read-ahead streaming, and session caching—without indexes or embeddings.

name: building-with-jev-skill
description: An agent skill for writing and improving programs that call Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, covering question design (Choice, Score, Noul), state structure, answer composition, confidence thresholds, and diagnosing wrong or low-confidence answers, targeting `jev-1.13` and installable via Claude Code plugin, skills CLI, or manual copy.

name: awesome-jev-usecases
description: An evidence-backed curated index of real-world use cases for Jev (TypeSafe AI System One), linking to repos, patterns, benchmarks, and measured results across LLM agents, routing, guardrails, RAG, reranking, calibration, structured output, and browser agents to help engineers evaluate proven applications.

name: jevpilot
description: A demo simulator where the Jev LLM pilots a car Autopilot-style by selecting from compact tables of sampled paths, road boundaries, traffic, and signals, with visualization of candidate paths, collision predictions, and API payloads, runnable locally with your own key.

name: Jevbox — a box of tools with common sense

name: HA-Jev
description: A Home Assistant integration that turns TypeSafe Jev decision-model answers (probabilities, choices, scores) into sensors, automation actions, and a voice-routing conversation agent, with request batching, per-question entity targeting, token budgets, and cost reporting.

name: blink
description: Blink is a Bun CLI that uses the Jev model to drive an ensemble of filesystem-walking agents that score path names and converge on files matching a natural-language query, reporting results as percentage-ranked tables with per-walker traces, cost/token metadata, and saved search outputs.

name: skillbox
description: Skillbox is a self-hosted, versioned skills library for AI agents that combines Markdown editing, immutable revisions, scoped permissions, revocable client keys, MCP/CLI access, imports/backups, and optional model-backed recommendations to manage, distribute, and audit reusable agent skills.

name: awesome-jev-examples

name: Learn Jev — Tutorials for TypeSafe AI's System One model
description: Independent, source-cited tutorials for TypeSafe AI's Jev System One model covering first call through production use, typed decision-making, confidence gating, and real cost math, while correcting overstated launch claims about hallucination, speed, and calibration.

description: A curated directory for TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model, collecting official SDKs and API docs, community-built apps and integrations, runnable offline examples and starters, plus cookbooks covering routing, retrieval, extraction, and evaluation patterns.

name: jev-ultrafast
description: jev-ultrafast is a browser agent that converts each DOM snapshot into an indexed element table and picks an operation and target in a single TypeSafe request (a small LLM only writes typed text), completing a Google Flights search in ~7 s without screenshots or site-specific scripts.

description: A zsh plugin that provides fish-style autosuggestions ranked by the Jev (TypeSafe) model over your last 100 distinct history entries, showing the top match in grey after the cursor (accept with → or ^E) via non-blocking per-keystroke requests with prefix/fuzzy modes and tunable score thresholds.

name: jev-review
description: A TypeSafe Jev–based code-review tool that orchestrates staged model judgments (file profiling, evidence selection, mechanism classification, severity scoring, conditional reviewer routing) over a Git diff or full codebase to flag correctness, security, reliability, compatibility, and test-coverage risks, presenting results in a localhost-only dashboard.

name: NanoJev
description: NanoJev is a 0.6B-parameter parallel decision model (Qwen3-0.6B with decision heads) that maps game states and questions directly to probability distributions over candidate actions—no token decoding—and ships with a checkpoint, an 18,760-question mixed-task dataset, and an inference service that plays ViZDoom, Maze, and Snake.

name: jev-desktop
description: Jev Desktop is a Codex plugin that keeps a bounded decision loop inside the existing Computer Use runtime—selecting one operation and compatible UI target per scoped TypeSafe request—so browser tab and native macOS app automation avoids per-click round-trips while Codex retains control of scope, permissions, prepared values, and verification.

name: jev-drone

name: jev

name: jevlike
